blindSummary:
This state/province remains the jurisdiction in the country with the deepest anti-discrimination apparatus, the largest visible queer community and the most institutionalised protection infrastructure. Ahead of the 2025 Pride celebrations (hundreds of thousands of attendees expected), organisers explicitly urged participants to stay vigilant amid a rise in attacks on LGBTQ+ events across the country, as reported by a foreign newspaper. The warning is event-specific; everyday institutional reception for a visitor here is the most hospitable in the country.

The local deviation is a small positive one against the country-wide average. A vigilance advisory pulls in a downward direction, but it concerns a single high-profile event, while the standing institutional protections - a state/province anti-discrimination office, the largest LGBTQ community infrastructure in the country and a long history of police cooperation with Pride - push up. Unlike a neighbouring state/province, this one has no public-administration hostility instruction and no record of joining a legislative initiative against the national self-identification law; the additional community infrastructure and enforcement capacity justify the small positive deviation.
